basis: Six-stage call audit framework supplied by ScaleSerum management (the 'Call Analysis parameter' sheet). Stage objectives, evaluation points and KPIs are transcribed from that sheet. Nothing here is invented.
how_to_configure: Every business value below is null on purpose. null means 'management has not decided'. Fill a value in, bump framework_version, redeploy - no Python changes are needed. scoring.py reports which of these were still null for every analysis it produces, so a placeholder can never be mistaken for a decision.
rating_scale_note: Maps each rating level to a fraction of score_max. null means no business mapping exists, so scoring.py derives one by spacing rating_levels uniformly over [0,1] and reports rating_scale_mode='uniform_placeholder'. Uniform spacing is a mechanical default, not a judgement about what 'adequate' is worth. To set a real one, supply an object keyed by rating level with fractions from 0.0 to 1.0.

weights.note: A null weight means equal weighting at that level. Set a positive number per stage/criterion to override, and flip the matching *_confirmed flag so the API stops reporting the weighting as a placeholder.

not_applicable_policy.note: What to do with a criterion or stage the call gave no opportunity for (e.g. Objection Handling when the customer raised no objection). 'exclude' drops it from the denominator; 'zero' scores it 0. 'exclude' is the neutral default because marking a rep down for something the customer never did is an artefact, not a finding. This is a business decision - confirmed:false until management rules.

bands_note: Score bands / pass-fail thresholds. null means none are configured, and the API returns band=null with band_reason='thresholds_not_configured'. Do NOT copy Script Lab's 90/70/50 ad-script bands here - they carry no authority for sales calls.

disposition_policy.note: Dispositions for which the six-stage evaluation should be skipped (a transcript is still produced). Empty on purpose: 'No Answer' and 'Invalid number' are the obvious candidates, but that is management's call. Values are matched case-insensitively against call_metadata.disposition.

requirements.vocal_tone: Needs an audio-derived transcript. A pasted text transcript carries no tone, energy or interruption information, so criteria tagged with this become not-applicable rather than being guessed at.
requirements.prior_interaction: Needs a recorded previous interaction, campaign or enquiry in the call context.
requirements.structured_programme: Only meaningful for products sold as a structured programme or certification.
requirements.payment_process: Only meaningful where enrolment or payment is completed by the representative on the call.

stages.name: Call Opening
stages.objective: Create a professional first impression and establish credibility.

criteria.name: Professional greeting delivered with confidence
Introduces self, organisation and designation
Confirms whether it is a convenient time to speak
Warm, energetic and engaging tone
Personalises using the customer's name or a previous interaction

stages.name: Purpose of the Call
stages.objective: Clearly communicate why the call has been made and set expectations.

criteria.name: States the reason for calling within the first minute
References the webinar, enquiry, profile review or previous interaction
Creates curiosity without overwhelming the customer
Transitions smoothly into the discussion

stages.name: Probing
stages.objective: Understand the customer's background, aspirations, challenges and decision-making criteria.

criteria.name: Understands current designation, industry and experience
Explores aspirations and longer-term ambitions
Identifies challenges or gaps
Practises active listening and asks relevant follow-up questions
Captures the customer's needs and decision criteria

stages.name: Product Pitching
stages.objective: Position the product or programme as the ideal solution aligned with the customer's goals.
stages.not_applicable_when: The call ended before any product or programme was presented.

criteria.name: Connects product benefits to the needs identified
Explains the programme structure and certifications
Highlights the unique value propositions
Explains ROI and value rather than only features
Uses success stories or practical examples
Avoids information overload

stages.name: Objection Handling
stages.objective: Address concerns confidently while maintaining the customer's trust.
stages.not_applicable_when: The customer raised no objection or concern during the call.

criteria.name: Listens without interrupting
Acknowledges the customer's concern
Clarifies the actual objection
Responds with logical and relevant solutions
Maintains a positive and calm tone

stages.name: Closing the Deal
stages.objective: Secure the customer's commitment and define the next step.
stages.not_applicable_when: The call ended before any close or next step could be attempted.

criteria.name: Identifies and acts on buying signals
Summarises the benefits discussed
Creates urgency where appropriate
Explains the payment or enrolment steps
Confirms the next action
Confirms timelines
Ends the call professionally with appreciation
